sample_unit: letter ratings (5 cases rated by primary care physicians, GPT-4 vs junior clinician letters)

links.outcome: GPT-4 vs junior clinician discharge letter quality rated by blinded primary care physicians
links.effect: GPT-4 higher on information provision (4.32 vs 3.70, P=.03); no significant differences in clarity, collegiality, conciseness, follow-up, or overall satisfaction (3.96 vs 3.62, P=.36).
links.quote: GPT-4 outperformed human counterparts in information provision (mean 4.32, SD 0.95 vs 3.70, SD 1.27; P=.03) and had no instances of hallucination.

links.outcome: GPT-4 letter quality compared against junior clinicians on same case records
links.effect: GPT-4 outperformed on information provision (P=.03); equivalent on clarity (P=.12), collegiality (P=.05), conciseness (P=.71), follow-up (P=.08), overall satisfaction (P=.36).
links.quote: Discharge letters written by GPT-4 had equivalent quality to those written by junior clinicians, without any hallucinations.

unlisted_practices: Safety-, content-, and style-specific prompt engineering for LLM-drafted discharge letters

screen.reason: The study compares GPT-4 generated discharge letters to those written by junior clinicians using fictional patient cases evaluated by primary care physicians, but does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard variation.
